lessons.title: What Would You Like?

items.text: Me gustaría un asiento junto a la ventana.
items.meaning: I would like a window seat.
items.example: Me gustaría un asiento junto a la ventana.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a window seat.

items.meaning: I would like a soft drink, please.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a soft drink, please.

items.meaning: Can I have a menu?
items.exampleMeaning: Can I have a menu?

items.meaning: I would like to change my flight.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like to change my flight.

items.meaning: I would like a pillow, please.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a pillow, please.

items.meaning: Can I order a taxi?
items.exampleMeaning: Can I order a taxi?

lessons.tip: Use 'me gustaría' or 'quisiera' to express what you would like. Both phrases are polite ways to make requests.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What would you like to order?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Me gustaría un asiento junto a la ventana.
dialogue.meaning: I would like a window seat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: And to drink?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I would like a soft drink, please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Can I offer you a menu?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, por favor. ¿Puedo tener un menú?
dialogue.meaning: Yes, please. Can I have a menu?

scenario.partnerRole: You are a flight attendant at an airport.
scenario.learnerRole: You are a passenger ordering items.
scenario.brief: Ask the passenger what they would like to order. Offer them a menu and take their requests.
scenario.goal: You need to order a drink and a seat.

lessons.title: Travel Documents

items.meaning: Where is my passport?
items.exampleMeaning: Where is my passport?

items.meaning: I need my boarding pass.
items.exampleMeaning: I need my boarding pass.

items.meaning: Here is my ID.
items.exampleMeaning: Here is my ID.

items.meaning: Do you have your visa?
items.exampleMeaning: Do you have your visa?

items.text: Mi vuelo sale en una hora.
items.meaning: My flight leaves in an hour.
items.example: Mi vuelo sale en una hora.
items.exampleMeaning: My flight leaves in an hour.

items.meaning: Where can I print my boarding pass?

items.exampleMeaning: Where can I print my boarding pass?

lessons.tip: Use '¿Dónde está?' to ask where something is. It's a useful phrase when looking for your things.

items.meaning: How long is the flight?

lessons.title: Confirming Details

items.meaning: Yes, I have my passport.
items.exampleMeaning: Yes, I have my passport.

items.meaning: No, I do not have my visa.
items.exampleMeaning: No, I do not have my visa.

items.text: Sí, mi vuelo sale en una hora.
items.meaning: Yes, my flight leaves in an hour.
items.example: Sí, mi vuelo sale en una hora.
items.exampleMeaning: Yes, my flight leaves in an hour.

items.meaning: Yes, I can change my seat.
items.exampleMeaning: Yes, I can change my seat.

items.text: No hay retraso en el vuelo.
items.meaning: There is no delay on the flight.
items.example: No hay retraso en el vuelo.
items.exampleMeaning: There is no delay on the flight.

items.text: Sí, la puerta de embarque está cerca.
items.meaning: Yes, the boarding gate is nearby.
items.example: Sí, la puerta de embarque está cerca.
items.exampleMeaning: Yes, the boarding gate is nearby.

lessons.tip: Use 'sí' for yes and 'no' for no. These are important for confirming details.
